About Me

A short history of my academic and professional experience

I'm a data and AI engineer with a background in physics and astrophysics and more than 20 years of experience in technology research, development, and innovation across the private sector, government, research laboratories, and universities. I'm at my best on problems that mix systems integration, data, and scientific reasoning.

Today I build the data infrastructure behind machine-learning research in diagnostic imaging (MRI, CT, ultrasound) at Nova Scotia Health: ETL pipelines, DICOM de-identification tooling, and annotation platforms for radiologists. Before that, I managed innovation-focused imaging R&D at the IWK Health Centre, including an ~$8M program building AI-based MRI tools with GE Healthcare Canada.

Earlier, I was CTO of a dental-technology startup, leading the team behind a cloud-based (AWS) SaaS analytics product used across North America, South America, and Europe, and before that I built Python test-automation software at BlackBerry for products used by millions.

My research career took me from stellar evolution models at Saint Mary's to the ANITA neutrino experiment at the University of Hawai'i: accelerator experiments at SLAC and two NASA long-duration balloon campaigns, in New Mexico and Antarctica. Along the way I made the top 100 of the Canadian Space Agency's astronaut recruitment campaign.
